title: Conduction classes, energy bands & forbidden gaps
subtitle: 30-order resistivity scale, opposite temperature laws, filled-band theorem, and key gap values.
takeaway: Metals warm UP in resistance (phonon scattering with fixed n); semiconductors cool DOWN in resistance (exponential carrier creation beats mobility loss)!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md Part 1, Part 2, sec. 3.1-3.2, E1, Q1-Q4

cards.title: 30-order resistivity scale & classification
items: Electrical resistivity spans ~30 orders of magnitude at 300 K: metals sit near 10^(-8) ohm.m, semiconductors span 10^(-5) to 10^4 ohm.m, and insulators reach 10^(18) ohm.m.
WHY / Magnitude alone overlaps at boundaries — what truly separates classes physically is whether carrier count n is FIXED (metal) or THERMALLY ACTIVATED across a gap (semiconductor)!
WATCH / Mystery sample E1 with rho ~ 10^(-2) ohm.m whose resistance FALLS when heated is an extrinsic/semiconducting sample, NEVER a nichrome alloy!

cards.title: Temperature coefficient alpha: metal vs Si vs NTC
items: Conductivity sigma = n e mu pulls two temperature levers in opposite directions: lattice phonon scattering lowers mu(T), whereas thermal excitation raises n(T).
WHY / In silicon, mild acoustic scattering mu ~ T^(-3/2) is completely crushed by exponential bond breaking exp(-Eg / 2kT), plunging resistivity steeply on warming!
WATCH / NTC thermistors exploit steep negative dR/dT for precision temperature sensing and inrush-current limiting; never treat a thermistor as ohmic over wide T!

cards.title: Allowed bands & why a filled band CANNOT conduct
items: Bringing N isolated atoms into a periodic crystal splits discrete atomic orbitals into N closely spaced crystal states forming valence (VB) and conduction (CB) bands.
WHY / Electric force F = -eE must shift electrons into adjacent empty k-states! A 100% full valence band has ZERO empty states — like a bumper-to-bumper parking lot, net current is identically zero!
WATCH / Never answer "electrons are too tightly bound to move" on JEE conceptual questions — answer "no unoccupied quantum states exist inside a filled band"!

cards.title: Forbidden band-gap benchmarks at 300 K
items: Forbidden energy gap Eg = Ec - Ev decides room-temperature carrier population relative to thermal energy kT = 25.9 meV at 300 K:
WHY / At 300 K, ni(C)/ni(Si) ~ exp[-(5.5 - 1.12)/(2 x 0.0259)] ~ 10^(-37) (essentially zero free electrons in diamond!), while ni(Ge)/ni(Si) ~ exp(+8.8) ~ 7 x 10^3!
WATCH / Carbon and silicon share Group-14 valence 4 and diamond tetrahedral bonding — ONLY smaller atomic spacing makes C 5.5 eV insulating vs Si 1.12 eV semiconducting!

title: Intrinsic carriers, doping, neutrality & mass action
subtitle: Half-gap thermal law, bond-swapping holes, Group-15/13 impurities, and np = ni^2 seesaw.
takeaway: Doped crystals are ELECTRICALLY NEUTRAL overall; n.p = ni^2 holds in thermal equilibrium for BOTH pure and doped semiconductors!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.3-3.4, E2-E3, Q3-Q6 & atomic-density audit

cards.title: Intrinsic carrier law & exact half-gap exponent
items: In pure crystal, thermal vibration breaks covalent bonds in pairs, so electron and hole concentrations are strictly equal: n = p = ni.
n_i(T) = \sqrt{N_c N_v}\,e^{-E_g / (2 k_B T)} \propto T^{3/2} e^{-E_g / (2 k_B T)}
WHY / Notice the factor 2 in exp(-Eg / 2kT)! Doubling T from 300 K to 600 K boosts exp(...) by exp(10.8) = 5.0e4 and T^(3/2) by 2.83 => total 1.43e5x jump!
WATCH / Audit check (Fig F27.5): for Si from 300 K to 400 K, exact ni(400)/ni(300) = (4/3)^(3/2) exp(5.41) = 346 (NOT 800)! Always keep 2kT in the denominator!

cards.title: Holes as positive quasiparticles & Group-15/13 doping
items: When a broken bond leaves an empty valence state, neighbouring valence electrons hop left under E right — making the vacancy drift right exactly like charge +e!
WHY / Audit note: Si diamond lattice has N_Si = 8 / (0.543 nm)^3 = 5.0 x 10^28 atoms/m^3, so Nd = 10^21 m^(-3) is 1 P per 5 x 10^7 Si atoms (1 ppm is 5 x 10^22 m^(-3))!
WATCH / Ionised donor cores P^+ and acceptor cores B^- are LOCKED in the crystal lattice — they set space charge rho(x) but carry ZERO conduction current!

cards.title: Bulk electrical neutrality & exact quadratic law
items: Every donated electron came from an initially neutral dopant atom, so an isolated n-type or p-type crystal has ZERO net charge!
n + N_a^- = p + N_d^+,\qquad n\,p = n_i^2
WHY / Whenever |Nd - Na| >> ni (standard extrinsic regime at 300 K), square root expands cleanly to majority n ~ Nd - Na while minority collapses to p = ni^2 / n!
WATCH / Classic JEE Advanced trap: if BOTH donors Nd and acceptors Na are added ("compensated Si"), net majority type is set by SIGN of (Nd - Na), and Nd = Na restores n = p = ni!

cards.title: Ten-order majority/minority seesaw (E3 & Q5)
items: Adding donors floods the crystal with electrons, increasing electron-hole recombination until minority holes drop inversely so the product np stays locked at ni^2:
N_d = 10^{21}\text{ m}^{-3} \Rightarrow n \approx 10^{21}\text{ m}^{-3},\ \ p = \frac{n_i^2}{N_d} = 2.25\times 10^{11}\text{ m}^{-3}
WHY / Dynamic equilibrium generation rate G(T) depends ONLY on temperature T, whereas recombination R ~ n.p: setting R = G forces n.p = ni(T)^2 even after heavy doping!
WATCH / Always convert cm^(-3) <-> m^(-3) cleanly BEFORE squaring ni: 1 cm^(-3) = 10^6 m^(-3), so ni(Si) = 1.5 x 10^10 cm^(-3) = 1.5 x 10^16 m^(-3)!

title: Drift, mobility, conductivity & Fick diffusion
subtitle: Dual-carrier drift currents, why e- and h+ currents ADD, and Einstein relation D/mu = kT/e.
takeaway: Under electric field E, electron and hole drift currents ADD (sigma = e(n mu_e + p mu_h)); under a concentration gradient, their diffusion currents SUBTRACT!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.5, E2-E3, Q7-Q8, P13-P14, P21

cards.title: Drift speed, mobility asymmetry & total conductivity
items: Under weak electric field E, electrons drift opposite E with v_e = mu_e E while positive holes drift along E with v_h = mu_h E — BOTH conventional currents point ALONG E!
WHY / Conduction-band electrons have lighter curvature effective mass and looser wavefunctions than valence-band bond-hopping holes, making NPN & NMOS faster than PNP & PMOS!
WATCH / Never subtract n mu_e - p mu_h in drift conductivity! (-e)(-v_e) + (+e)(+v_h) = +e(n v_e + p v_h) — opposite charges moving in opposite directions ADD!

cards.title: Intrinsic vs doped silicon numbers (E2, E3 & P21)
items: Pure silicon conducts like wet stone; trace Group-15/13 doping boosts conductivity by 5 orders of magnitude without altering crystal geometry:
WHY / Minority hole contribution e p mu_h ~ 1.7e-9 S/m is 10 orders smaller than 21.6 S/m — drop the minority term instantly whenever doping exceeds 100 ni!
WATCH / Minimum conductivity of a doped semiconductor does NOT occur at n = p = ni! Minimising n mu_e + (ni^2/n) mu_h gives p-type minimum at p = ni sqrt(mu_e / mu_h)!

cards.title: Fick diffusion current & sign rule
items: Even when E = 0, random thermal motion drives net particle flux from high to low concentration (-D dn/dx), creating diffusion current density:
WHY / If BOTH electrons and holes decrease toward +x (dn/dx < 0, dp/dx < 0, e.g. surface illumination), both diffuse right — so J_p points +x while J_n points -x!
WATCH / Watch the PLUS sign on J_{n,diff} = +e Dn (dn/dx) vs MINUS sign on J_{p,diff} = -e Dp (dp/dx) — opposite of drift because same-direction particle fluxes carry opposite charges!

cards.title: Total transport equations & Einstein relation
items: Combining drift and diffusion for each carrier species and enforcing zero net current in thermal equilibrium links diffusion constant D directly to mobility mu:
J_n = e n\mu_e E + e D_n\frac{dn}{dx},\qquad J_p = e p\mu_h E - e D_p\frac{dp}{dx}
WHY / Both scattering relaxation time tau and thermal energy kT govern random walks AND field drift — their ratio D/mu depends ONLY on temperature T!
WATCH / In Si at 300 K: Dn = 0.135 x 0.0259 = 3.50 x 10^(-3) m^2/s (35 cm^2/s) and Dp = 1.24 x 10^(-3) m^2/s (12.4 cm^2/s) — quick sanity numbers for Olympiad checks!

title: p-n junction equilibrium, barrier hill & space charge
subtitle: Uncovered ion dipole, Boltzmann contact potential V0, and aligned rho(x), E(x), V(x) curves.
takeaway: Built-in E_bi points from n (+Nd ions) to p (-Na ions), so n-side sits HIGHER in electrostatic potential by V0 — yet a voltmeter across the terminals ALWAYS reads ZERO!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.6, C7-C8, OL2-OL3, P23

cards.title: Depletion formation & drift-diffusion cancellation
items: Joining p and n silicon triggers massive majority diffusion across x = 0, uncovering immobile negative acceptors (-e Na) on p-side and positive donors (+e Nd) on n-side.
N_a\,x_p = N_d\,x_n\ \ (\text{total space charge } Q_+ + Q_- = 0\text{!})
WHY / Overall dipole neutrality Na xp = Nd xn forces the depletion region to penetrate DEEPER into the LIGHTLY doped side (if Na >> Nd, almost all W sits inside n)!
WATCH / Trap 2: "The depletion region has net positive/negative charge" -> FALSE! Equal +Q and -Q layers cancel identically!

cards.title: Built-in contact potential V0 from Boltzmann
items: Integrating e n mu_e (-dV/dx) + e Dn (dn/dx) = 0 from neutral p-bulk to neutral n-bulk yields the exact built-in barrier height V0:
WHY / Typical built-in barriers sit just below Eg/e: ~0.65-0.75 V in Si, ~0.25-0.35 V in Ge, and ~1.1-1.2 V in GaAs!
WATCH / Why can you NOT power a bulb with V0 = 0.7 V? Metal wire contacts at both ends create equal and opposite contact potentials summing to ZERO around any closed loop!

cards.title: Exact aligned rho(x), E(x) & V(x) profiles
items: Integrating Poisson dE/dx = rho / eps twice across [-xp, +xn] connects rectangular charge blocks to triangular field and parabolic S-curve potential:
WHY / Peak electric field |E_max| sits RIGHT AT THE METALLURGICAL JUNCTION x = 0 (~5 x 10^5 V/m across 2.5 um!), and drops linearly to zero at edges -xp and +xn!
WATCH / Electron potential energy U_e(x) = -e V(x) is UPSIDE DOWN relative to electrostatic V(x): V(x) rises p -> n, so band edges Ec(x), Ev(x) step UP n -> p!

cards.title: Depletion width scaling W ~ sqrt(V0 + VR)
items: Applying external voltage V shifts the potential barrier to (V0 - V) in forward bias or (V0 + VR) under reverse voltage VR:
WHY / Forward bias shrinks W and lowers the hill for exponential majority injection; reverse bias widens W and raises the hill to V0 + VR!
WATCH / Q9 & P23 check: quadrupling VR from 1 V to 4 V doubles W ONLY when VR >> V0! With V0 = 0.7 V, exact ratio is sqrt((0.7+4)/(0.7+1)) = 1.66x!

title: Shockley diode law, 60 mV rule, dynamic rd & breakdown
subtitle: Exponential forward conduction, decade ladder, static vs dynamic resistance, Zener vs avalanche.
takeaway: Every +60 mV forward bias multiplies ideal diode current by 10x at 300 K; small-signal dynamic resistance is rd = VT / I = 26 mV / I_DC!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.7, E5, Q10-Q11, P7, P15, P27

cards.title: Shockley equation & the 60 mV-per-decade ladder
items: Lowering the junction hill from V0 to V0 - V boosts majority carrier injection over the barrier by exp(eV / kT), yielding Shockley's diode equation:
I = I_0\!\left(e^{V / (\eta V_T)} - 1\right),\qquad V_T = \frac{k_B T}{e} = 25.9\text{ mV}\ (300\text{ K})
WHY / Example E5 & Q10: 1 mA at 0.60 V -> 10 mA at 0.66 V -> 100 mA at 0.72 V -> 1 A at 0.78 V! The "0.7 V knee" is simply where nanoamps cross into milliamps!
WATCH / Real discrete Si diodes often have recombination factor eta ~ 1.5-2 at low current (90-120 mV/decade), whereas BJT collector current IC(VBE) obeys pure eta = 1!

cards.title: Static DC resistance R_DC vs AC dynamic resistance r_d
items: JEE Main & NEET frequently test small voltage ripples superimposed on a DC forward diode bias — NEVER divide V / I when they ask for dynamic resistance!
WHY / At I = 2 mA and V = 0.70 V, static R_DC = 350 ohm, whereas AC slope resistance is rd = 26 mV / 2 mA = 13 ohm — 27 times smaller!
WATCH / Near V = 0 (|V| << VT), exp(V/VT) - 1 ~ V/VT becomes linear and ohmic with zero-bias slope resistance r0 = VT / I0!

cards.title: Reverse saturation I0 & its 10-degree doubling rule
items: For reverse bias V < -4 VT (~ -0.1 V), exp(V/VT) vanishes and reverse current saturates at -I0 (nA in Si, uA in Ge), independent of reverse voltage before breakdown.
WHY / Notice NO factor of 2 in exp(-Eg / kT) because minority concentration p_{n0} = ni^2 / Nd scales as ni SQUARED! I0 roughly DOUBLES every +7 to +10 K rise!
WATCH / P27 subtlety: at fixed V = 0.60 V, heating shrinks exp(V/VT) yet TOTAL diode current STILL RISES on heating because I0 ~ exp(-Eg/kT) explodes faster, dropping V_knee by ~2 mV/K!

cards.title: Zener tunnelling (<5 V) vs avalanche breakdown (>6 V)
items: Two distinct physical mechanisms trigger sharp reverse current rise at breakdown voltage V_BR:
WHY / Warming shrinks Eg so Zener tunnelling gets EASIER (dVz/dT < 0), whereas warming shortens mean free path so avalanche needs MORE voltage (dV_BR/dT > 0)!
WATCH / Around Vz = 5.1-5.6 V both effects cancel to give dVz/dT ~ 0 — why 5.1 V and 5.6 V Zeners are precision industry favourites (P17)!

title: Half/full-wave rectifiers, capacitor ripple & clippers
subtitle: Exact DC, RMS, efficiency, form factor, PIV, bridge double drop, filter ripple, and clippers/clampers.
takeaway: Full-wave bridge drops TWO knees (Vp - 1.4 V) with PIV = Vp and ripple f_rip = 2f; smoothing ripple is dV = I / (2fC) full-wave vs I / (fC) half-wave!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.8, E6-E7, Q12-Q14, P8, P16, P24

cards.title: Half-wave vs full-wave rectifier benchmark table
items: For sinusoidal input v(t) = Vp sin(wt) feeding pure load RL (ideal diodes):
WHY / AC ripple factor r = sqrt((Vrms/Vdc)^2 - 1) drops from 1.21 (half-wave: more AC than DC!) down to 0.482 (full-wave), and fundamental ripple frequency DOUBLES from f to 2f!
WATCH / PIV (Peak Inverse Voltage) trap: half-wave = Vp; 4-diode bridge = Vp; 2-diode CENTRE-TAP full-wave = 2 Vp across the blocking diode!

cards.title: Real silicon diode drops: 4-diode bridge vs centre-tap
items: When transformer peak Vp is modest (e.g. 5-12 V), always check whether the question specifies silicon diodes (V_gamma = 0.7 V) or ideal diodes:
\mathrm{Bridge\ (4\ diodes):}\ \ V_{p,\mathrm{out}} = V_p - 2 V_\gamma \approx V_p - 1.4\text{ V}
\mathrm{Centre\text{-}tap\ (2\ diodes):}\ \ V_{p,\mathrm{out}} = V_p - V_\gamma \approx V_p - 0.7\text{ V}
WHY / Trace the diamond loop: during positive half-cycle D1 -> RL -> D3 conduct IN SERIES; during negative half-cycle D2 -> RL -> D4 conduct IN SERIES!
WATCH / If ONE diode in a 4-diode bridge burns OPEN, it degrades cleanly into a HALF-WAVE rectifier (f_rip = f, Vdc halves); if one shorts, it shorts the AC transformer!

cards.title: Shunt capacitor filter & sawtooth ripple equation
items: Placing large capacitor C in parallel with RL charges C to peak Vp every cycle, then discharges nearly linearly at rate dV/dt = -I_L / C for time T_dis:
\Delta V_{\mathrm{FW}} \approx \frac{I_L}{2 f C} = \frac{V_p}{2 f R_L C},\qquad \Delta V_{\mathrm{HW}} \approx \frac{I_L}{f C}
WHY / E7 & P16 check: full-wave 50 Hz, I = 100 mA, C = 1000 uF gives dV = 0.1 / (100 x 10^-3) = 1.0 V; 50 mA with 470 uF gives dV = 1.06 V!
WATCH / Match 2f vs f CAREFULLY! Full-wave recharges C twice per mains period (T/2 = 10 ms at 50 Hz), half-wave only once (T = 20 ms -> twice the ripple)!

cards.title: Clippers (limiters), DC clampers & peak detectors
items: Diodes reshape AC waveforms either by slicing above/below a threshold (clipper: resistor + diode) or shifting DC baseline without distortion (clamper: capacitor + diode):
WHY / Always solve ANY clamper in two steps: (1) find the half-cycle that turns the diode ON first to lock capacitor voltage V_C; (2) write KVL v_out = v_in +/- V_C on the OFF half-cycle!
WATCH / A clamper NEVER alters peak-to-peak swing 2 Vp of the input wave — it translates the entire waveform vertically from [-Vp, +Vp] to [0, +2 Vp] (or [-2 Vp, 0])!

title: Zener regulators, LEDs, photodiodes & solar cells
subtitle: Two-sided Zener resistor squeeze, direct vs indirect bandgaps, and 4-quadrant PV physics.
takeaway: Size Rs at (Vin,min & IL,max), then check Zener power PZ,max at (Vin,max & IL = 0 disconnected load!); solar cells operate in Quadrant IV (V > 0, I < 0)!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.9, E8-E9, Q16-Q20, P9, P12, P17-P18

cards.title: Zener shunt regulator & worst-case two-sided squeeze
items: Reverse-biased Zener diode clamps load voltage at V_out = Vz PROVIDED Zener current stays between knee minimum IZ,min and power limit IZ,max = PZ,max / Vz:
I_R = \frac{V_{\mathrm{in}} - V_Z}{R_s} = I_Z + I_L,\qquad R_{s,\max} = \frac{V_{\mathrm{in,\min}} - V_Z}{I_{L,\max} + I_{Z,\min}}
I_{Z,\max} = \frac{V_{\mathrm{in,\max}} - V_Z}{R_s} - I_{L,\min}\ \ \bigl(\text{worst case at } I_L = 0\text{!}\bigr)
WHY / E8 & Q16: Vin = 12 V, Vz = 5 V, IL = 0..50 mA, IZ,min = 5 mA => Rs <= 7 / 0.055 = 127 ohm; picking 120 ohm gives no-load IZ = 58.3 mA, PZ = 0.29 W!
WATCH / Before writing V_out = Vz in ANY JEE problem, ALWAYS check Thevenin open-circuit voltage V_th = Vin RL / (Rs + RL) >= Vz! If V_th < Vz, the Zener is OFF and V_out = V_th!

cards.title: Light-Emitting Diodes (LEDs) & why silicon fails
items: Forward-biasing a heavily doped direct-bandgap junction injects electrons & holes that recombine radiatively across Eg, emitting monochromatic photons:
WHY / Visible anchors: Red 620-680 nm (1.8-2.0 eV, GaAsP), Green 550 nm (2.25 eV, GaP), Blue 470 nm (2.64 eV, InGaN); IR remotes use GaAs (1.42 eV -> 873 nm)!
WATCH / Why NO silicon LEDs (E9 & Q18)? Two fatal reasons: (1) Eg = 1.12 eV -> 1107 nm infrared, AND (2) Si has an INDIRECT gap (momentum mismatch goes into lattice heat phonons)!

cards.title: Photodiodes (Quadrant III reverse-bias light meters)
items: Illuminating a reverse-biased p-n junction with photons hv > Eg generates electron-hole pairs inside/near the depletion region that E_bi sweeps apart instantly:
WHY / Why reverse bias instead of forward? Reverse bias (1) crushes dark current I0 to nanoamps so tiny light shifts stand out, AND (2) widens W -> shrinks Cj for nanosecond speed!
WATCH / Photons with lambda > 1240 / Eg pass straight through the crystal unabsorbed — a silicon photodiode is completely blind beyond ~1100 nm!

cards.title: Solar photovoltaic cells (Quadrant IV zero-bias power)
items: With NO external battery, photogenerated carriers swept across the junction pile holes on p and electrons on n, forward-biasing the cell to deliver real electrical power:
I(V) = I_0\!\left(e^{V / V_T} - 1\right) - I_L,\qquad V_{\mathrm{oc}} = V_T\ln\!\left(1 + \frac{I_L}{I_0}\right)
WHY / Choose active layer with Eg ~ 1.1-1.5 eV (Si 1.12 eV, GaAs 1.42 eV, CdTe 1.45 eV) and high optical absorption alpha so maximum solar spectrum converts into power!
WATCH / Q20 favourite JEE question: "A solar cell operates in Quadrant IV because it generates power (V > 0 while current exits the positive p-terminal)" — NEVER draw external bias!

title: Bipolar junction transistor (BJT): gains & modes
subtitle: Asymmetric doping geometry, alpha-beta identities, saturation test, and mode table.
takeaway: IC = beta IB holds ONLY in forward-active mode! ALWAYS test beta*IB against (VCC - 0.2 V)/RC FIRST — whichever is SMALLER wins!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.10, E10, Q21-Q23, P10, P19, P25

cards.title: Asymmetric E-B-C design & current law
items: An NPN transistor is NOT two back-to-back discrete diodes: Emitter is heavily doped (n++), Base is ultra-thin & lightly doped (p), and Collector has the largest area (n):
WHY / Thin lightly doped base lets 98-99.5% of injected emitter electrons diffuse across to the collector before recombining (alpha = 0.99 => beta = 99, E10 & P10)!
WATCH / Collector has the LARGEST physical area NOT for doping, but to dissipate heat P_C = V_CE I_C (~99% of transistor heating occurs at the reverse-biased B-C junction)!

cards.title: Four operating modes set by E-B & C-B junction biases
items: Every BJT question starts by classifying the bias polarities of Emitter-Base (EBJ) and Collector-Base (CBJ) junctions:
WHY / Reverse-active (EBJ OFF, CBJ ON) swaps emitter and collector roles with terrible gain beta_rev ~ 0.1-2 because the collector was never heavily doped to inject!
WATCH / Swapping Emitter and Collector pins of an NPN transistor on a breadboard puts it into reverse-active mode — circuit barely works instead of burning out!

cards.title: 20-second saturation test (Q23 & P25 killer trap!)
items: Given VCC, collector resistor RC, base current IB, and gain beta, NEVER write IC = beta IB blindly — run this 3-step check first:
WHY / Q23 proof: VCC = 5 V, RC = 1 k, beta = 100, IB = 100 uA => beta*IB = 10 mA gives impossible VCE = 5 - 10 = -5 V! True saturated IC = (5 - 0.2)/1k = 4.8 mA!
WATCH / Marking-scheme penalty warning (Part 12): writing IC = beta IB in saturation loses ALL numerical marks even with flawless arithmetic!

cards.title: DC load line & Q-point placement
items: Kirchhoff's voltage loop on the collector side imposes a straight line across the transistor's output characteristic family:
V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C(R_C + R_E) \Rightarrow I_C = -\frac{V_{CE}}{R_C + R_E} + \frac{V_{CC}}{R_C + R_E}
WHY / Placing quiescent operating point Q near the centre (VCE,Q ~ VCC / 2) maximises symmetric peak-to-peak undistorted output swing before hitting cutoff or saturation clipping!
WATCH / Where does amplified signal power come from (C12 & Trap 8)? 100% from the DC battery VCC — the base signal merely modulates the valve opening!

title: Common-emitter amplifier, gains & BJT switch design
subtitle: Small-signal gm, voltage/power gain, 180-deg phase inversion, and hard-saturated load switches.
takeaway: CE amplifier inverts phase by 180 deg with Av = -beta RC / r_in = -gm RC and Ap = beta * |Av|; a digital BJT switch lives ONLY in Cutoff and Saturation!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.11, E11, Q24, P25

cards.title: Common-emitter (CE) small-signal gains & transconductance
items: Around active Q-point (IC, VCE), tiny input wiggle dV_BE produces dI_B = dV_BE / r_in and collector wiggle dI_C = beta dI_B = gm dV_BE:
g_m = \frac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta V_{BE}} = \frac{I_C}{V_T},\qquad r_\pi = \frac{\Delta V_{BE}}{\Delta I_B} = \frac{\beta}{g_m} = \frac{\beta V_T}{I_C}
WHY / MINUS sign in Av = -gm RC means 180-deg phase inversion (Q24): rising Vin drives higher IC, larger I_C R_C drop, and LOWER output voltage VCE = VCC - IC RC!
WATCH / Notice power gain Ap = A_i |A_v| scales as BETA SQUARED! For beta = 100 and RC = R_in, |Av| = 100 while signal power gain is Ap = 10,000 (+40 dB)!

cards.title: CB vs CE vs CC configuration comparison
items: Only Common-Emitter gives BOTH high current gain (beta) and high voltage gain (gm RC), making CE the universal workhorse stage:
WHY / Emitter follower (CC) has voltage gain +1 (0-deg phase) and high input / low output impedance — ideal unity-gain buffer driving heavy low-resistance loads!
WATCH / Adding an unbypassed emitter resistor RE stabilizes Q-point thermally and sets rock-solid voltage gain Av ~ -RC / RE independent of transistor beta spread!

cards.title: Transfer curve Vout(Vin) & CMOS/RTL NOT gate origin
items: Sweeping DC input Vin from 0 V to VCC sweeps Vout = VCE across three sharp zones that define BOTH linear amplification and digital inversion:
WHY / Analog amplifiers bias RIGHT IN THE MIDDLE steep linear slope; digital logic gates slam cleanly between the TWO FLAT ENDS (0 V and VCC) where transistor power is tiny!
WATCH / In active region P_transistor = VCE IC is maximum (hot!); in Cutoff (IC = 0) and hard Saturation (VCE ~ 0.2 V), switch dissipation I_C V_{CE} is nearly ZERO!

cards.title: Designing a saturated BJT lamp/relay switch (E11 & P25)
items: To switch load I_{C,sat} cleanly from logic high V_{in} (e.g. 5.0 V MCU pin), force base current safely above the minimum threshold I_{B,min} = I_{C,sat} / beta:
WHY / E11 check: 5 V supply, 100 mA lamp, beta = 100 needs IB >= 1.0 mA => RB <= (5 - 0.7)/1 mA = 4.3 kOhm (pick 2.2 kOhm for 2x overdrive); lamp gets 5.0 - 0.2 = 4.8 V!
WATCH / When driving inductive relay/motor coils with a BJT switch, ALWAYS place a flyback diode anti-parallel across the coil so L(dI/dt) turn-off spikes never puncture VCE!

title: Diode/transistor logic circuits, truth tables & waveforms
subtitle: DL/RTL hardware implementations, all seven gate truth tables, and JEE pulse-timing traces.
takeaway: Diode anodes at inputs + pull-DOWN resistor = OR gate; diode cathodes at inputs + pull-UP resistor = AND gate; add a CE transistor stage to invert into NOR / NAND!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.12, C14, Q15, Q25

cards.title: Hardware Diode Logic (DL) & Transistor Inverter (RTL)
items: JEE Main regularly draws raw diode-resistor-transistor schematics and asks which Boolean gate they implement — identify the pull resistor FIRST:
WHY / In Diode AND, if EITHER input A = 0 V, its diode conducts and clamps output Y down to 0.7 V (Logic 0); Y stays HIGH (+VCC) ONLY when BOTH A = 1 AND B = 1!
WATCH / Two NPN transistors in PARALLEL sharing collector pull-up RC form a NOR gate; two NPN transistors in SERIES under pull-up RC form a NAND gate!

cards.title: Complete truth tables of all 7 standard gates
items: For input pairs (A, B) ordered strictly as (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1), memorise each gate's 4-bit output signature cold:
WHY / Fast verbal shortcuts: AND = "all 1s"; OR = "any 1"; NAND = "0 ONLY at 1,1"; NOR = "1 ONLY at 0,0"; XOR = "inequality / odd-parity detector"; XNOR = "equality comparator"!
WATCH / Tying one input of XOR to a control line C makes a programmable inverter: A xor 0 = A (buffer), whereas A xor 1 = NOT A (inverter)!

cards.title: Why binary logic beats decimal hardware (C14)
items: Digital circuits encode 0 and 1 as wide voltage bands separated by a forbidden transition zone, rejecting power noise, crosstalk, and device tolerances:
A \oplus B = A\overline{B} + \overline{A}B,\qquad A \odot B = \overline{A\oplus B} = AB + \overline{A}\,\overline{B}
WHY / Every CMOS logic gate regenerates degraded levels right back to clean 0 V or VDD rails — errors do NOT accumulate across 100 stages!
WATCH / Associativity superpower: multi-input XOR (A xor B xor C) outputs 1 whenever an ODD number of inputs equal 1 — instant parity checker!

cards.title: Solving JEE digital pulse-train waveform problems
items: When given square-wave timing graphs A(t), B(t) and 4 candidate output graphs Y(t), NEVER trace intermediate gates sloppily by eye:
1.\ \text{Slice time into clock slots } t_1, t_2, \dots, t_k
WHY / Simplifying the gate network algebraically FIRST (e.g. spotting Y = A + B' in 5 seconds!) eliminates 100% of intermediate-node copy errors under exam pressure!
WATCH / Watch whether HIGH voltage is drawn UP or whether negative logic is stated in the stem — read vertical axis labels before ticking options!

title: Boolean algebra, De Morgan, universal NAND/NOR & adders
subtitle: Absorption laws, bubble-pushing De Morgan rules, minimum NAND/NOR counts, and half/full adders.
takeaway: Minimum gate count sequence: NAND builds [NOT, AND, OR, XOR, XNOR] in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] gates; NOR reverses AND/OR & XOR/XNOR to [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] gates!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.12, E12, Q26-Q28, P11, P26

cards.title: Boolean algebra shortcuts that collapse 5 lines to 1
items: Beyond commutativity and distributivity, three non-ordinary identities do 90% of all JEE Boolean simplifications:
A + A = A,\quad A + 1 = 1,\quad A + \overline{A} = 1,\quad A\overline{A} = 0
WHY / Test A + A'B = A + B quickly: if A = 1, both equal 1; if A = 0, LHS = B and RHS = B — identical on EVERY row in 2 seconds!
WATCH / Never cancel terms like ordinary algebra (A + B = A + C does NOT imply B = C in Boolean algebra)! Always double-check any tricky reduction on the 4 truth rows!

cards.title: De Morgan's theorems & graphical bubble-pushing
items: Break an overbar, flip the operator between AND (.) and OR (+)! Graphically: a NAND gate IS an inverted-input OR gate; a NOR gate IS an inverted-input AND gate:
WHY / Whenever two inversion bubbles meet head-to-head on the same wire, they CANCEL cleanly (double complement A'' = A) — instant visual reduction of multi-NAND schematics!
WATCH / Watch bar height carefully! OVERLINE(A + B) != OVERLINE(A) + OVERLINE(B)! Only split an overbar AT THE EXACT MOMENT you flip (+) <-> (.)!

cards.title: Universal NAND & NOR minimum-gate counts
items: Both NAND and NOR are functionally complete (universal). Memorise BOTH construction formulas AND exact minimum 2-input gate counts:
WHY / Optimal 4-NAND XOR ingeniously reuses first shared gate G1 = NAND(A, B) to compute NAND(NAND(A, G1), NAND(B, G1)) = A xor B without two extra NOT gates!
WATCH / Classic JEE trap: naive student builds A'B + AB' with 5 NANDs and ticks "5" — MINIMUM number of 2-input NAND gates for XOR is ALWAYS 4!

cards.title: Binary arithmetic: Half Adder & Full Adder (E12, Q28, P26)
items: Adding two 1-bit binary numbers A + B produces 2-bit output (Carry C, Sum S); adding carry-in C_in from a lower column makes a Full Adder:
\text{Half Adder:}\ \ S = A\oplus B,\quad C = A\cdot B\ \ (5\text{ NAND})
\mathrm{Full\ Adder:}\ \ S = A\oplus B\oplus C_{\mathrm{in}},\quad C_{\mathrm{out}} = A B + C_{\mathrm{in}}(A\oplus B)
WHY / Check 1 + 1 in Half Adder: S = 1 xor 1 = 0, C = 1 . 1 = 1 -> binary "10" (= decimal 2)! Two Half Adders + one OR gate build a complete 1-bit Full Adder (9 NANDs min)!
WATCH / Half subtractor calculating A - B has the EXACT SAME Difference bit D = A xor B, changing ONLY Borrow = A' . B!

title: Master JEE triage, multi-diode networks & 10 exam traps
subtitle: Rapid formula selector, multi-diode open-circuit solver, LED lookup, and ten fatal traps.
takeaway: Mode BEFORE algebra on every diode, Zener, and transistor problem — one 5-second open-circuit / saturation check saves full marks!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md Parts 7-9, Traps 1-10, Part 14 checklist

cards.title: Multi-diode circuit solver (Part 7.3 gold standard)
items: When a network contains two or more diodes sharing a node (e.g. diodes D1 at +1 V and D2 at +3 V feeding one pull-down resistor), DO NOT guess randomly:
WHY / Example: anodes at +3 V and +1 V joined to ground via R (ideal diodes) -> +3 V diode turns ON first, clamping cathode node to +3 V so the +1 V diode is REVERSE biased at -2 V (OFF)!
WATCH / NEVER leave a solved circuit with an "ON" diode carrying negative current I < 0 or an "OFF" diode sitting at forward V > V_knee!

cards.title: Core silicon 300 K anchor constants (memorise cold!)
items: Carry these eight room-temperature numbers into every JEE Main, JEE Advanced, and NSEP paper for instant 5-second sanity checks:
V_T = 25.9\text{ mV},\quad \Delta V_{10\times} = 60\text{ mV/dec},\quad hc = 1240\ \mathrm{eV\cdot nm}
WHY / Even when a problem gives slightly rounded data (VT = 25 mV or ni = 10^16 m^-3), knowing exact physical scales catches 10^6 unit slips instantly!
WATCH / Germanium numbers differ noticeably: Eg = 0.66 eV, V_knee ~ 0.3 V, V_{CE,sat} ~ 0.1 V, and much larger leakage current I0 (uA vs nA)!

cards.title: Five conceptual JEE traps examiners repeat every year
items: 1. "n-type silicon is negatively charged" -> FALSE! Mobile e- + fixed P^+ sum to ZERO net charge!
2. "Depletion region carries net charge" -> FALSE! Equal +e Nd xn and -e Na xp dipole!
3. "Voltmeter across p-n diode reads 0.7 V" -> FALSE! Contact potentials cancel to 0 V!
WHY / Raising forward LED current emits MORE photons/sec of the SAME wavelength 1240/Eg; changing colour requires changing semiconductor alloy composition x!
WATCH / 5. "Transistor amplifies energy" -> FALSE! DC power supply VCC provides the energy; transistor merely valves collector flow!

cards.title: Five circuit-algebra JEE traps to check before submitting
items: Run this 30-second checklist across your numerical working before locking options:
\mathrm{Bridge\ drop} = 2 V_\gamma\ \big|\ \ \Delta V_{\mathrm{FW}} = \frac{I}{2 f C}\ \text{vs}\ \Delta V_{\mathrm{HW}} = \frac{I}{f C}
\text{Check } V_{\mathrm{th}} > V_Z,\ \ P_{Z,\max}\big|_{I_L=0},\ \ \beta I_B\text{ vs } I_{C,\mathrm{sat}}
WHY / Nearly 80% of all lost marks in JEE electronics come NOT from hard physics, but from applying IC = beta IB in saturation or forgetting 2f vs f in ripple!
WATCH / Always check cm^(-3) vs m^(-3) BEFORE using sigma = n e mu or n p = ni^2 — missing 10^6 gives answers off by 1,000,000x!

title: Scaled Bohr donors, Fermi level & intrinsic crossover
subtitle: Hydrogenic impurity derivation, valley-anisotropy honesty factor, Fermi shifts, and 560 K ceiling.
takeaway: Scaled Bohr gives Ed = 13.6 (m*/m) / kappa^2 = 26 meV ~ kT and a* = 2.4 nm in Si (measured 45 meV due to 6-valley anisotropy); Si loses doping above ~560 K!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.4, E4, OL1, OL12, P22, P28

cards.title: Hydrogenic impurity model (OL1, E4, P22 & P28)
items: An extra fifth valence electron of P orbiting a +e core inside crystal permittivity kappa = eps_r moves with band effective mass m*, rescaling Bohr's atom cleanly:
WHY / Because a* = 2.4 nm spans ~4.4 cubic lattice cells (a_Si = 0.543 nm; ~9 bond lengths!), averaging over hundreds of Si atoms makes macroscopic dielectric screening kappa valid!

WATCH / Olympiad marking-rubric MUST-WRITE honesty line (Part 12): measured Si:P is 45 meV (1.7x higher) because silicon's 6 anisotropic conduction valleys & central-cell potential deviate from isotropic hydrogen!

cards.title: Fermi-Dirac distribution & Fermi-level shift with doping
items: Occupation probability of state E is governed by Fermi-Dirac statistics; when E - EF >> kT, it reduces to Boltzmann factor exp(-(E - EF)/kT):
f(E) = \frac{1}{e^{(E - E_F)/(k_B T)} + 1},\qquad E_{F,i} = \frac{E_c + E_v}{2} + \frac{3}{4}k_B T\ln\!\left(\frac{m_h^*}{m_e^*}\right)
n = n_i\,e^{(E_F - E_i)/(k_B T)},\qquad p = n_i\,e^{(E_i - E_F)/(k_B T)}
WHY / Multiplying n and p cancels EF identically to prove np = ni^2! n-doping shifts EF UP toward Ec by kT ln(Nd/ni); p-doping shifts EF DOWN toward Ev by kT ln(Na/ni)!
WATCH / At T -> 0 K in pure crystal, intrinsic Fermi level sits EXACTLY midway at (Ec + Ev)/2 regardless of mass asymmetry m_h* != m_e*!

cards.title: Freeze-out (<120 K), extrinsic plateau & intrinsic ceiling
items: Plotting log n vs 1000/T across cryogenic to high temperature reveals three distinct physical regimes in doped silicon:
1.\ \text{Freeze-out }(k_B T \ll E_d):\ n \propto e^{-E_d/(2 k_B T)}
3.\ \text{Intrinsic }(n_i > N_d):\ n \approx n_i \propto T^{3/2} e^{-E_g/(2 k_B T)}
WHY / Notice factor 2 in BOTH slopes on an Arrhenius plot: steep high-T slope measures -Eg/(2k), shallow cryogenic slope measures -Ed/(2k)!
WATCH / In the extrinsic saturation window (near 300 K), n = Nd is constant while mu ~ T^(-3/2) falls — so lightly doped Si actually shows a SMALL POSITIVE dR/dT until ni wakes up!

cards.title: When silicon devices forget their doping (OL12 exact)
items: Once thermal generation raises ni(T) up to dopant density Nd, p-n junctions lose rectification (V0 -> 0) and transistors fail completely:
WHY / Wide-bandgap semiconductors SiC (Eg = 3.26 eV) and GaN (Eg = 3.4 eV) push this thermal ceiling well past 600 deg C — why EV inverters & jet-engine sensors use SiC/GaN!
WATCH / Germanium (Eg = 0.66 eV) hits intrinsic washout right around ~90-100 deg C — why early 1950s Ge transistors failed in hot summer equipment and Si won!

title: Boltzmann diode derivation, Poisson step junction & varactors
subtitle: Minority injection law, 2-sided vs 1-sided depletion audit, and voltage-tuned RF varactors.
takeaway: Watch 1-sided vs symmetric step junctions: W_1side = sqrt(2 eps V_tot / eN), whereas symmetric Na = Nd = N has W_sym = sqrt(4 eps V_tot / eN) = sqrt(2) W_1side!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md OL2-OL3, P23, P27, P29 & step-junction audit

cards.title: Shockley equation from Boltzmann boundary law (OL2)
items: In equilibrium, minority electrons at the p-side depletion edge equal n_{p0} = n_{n0} exp(-eV0/kT). Forward bias V lowers barrier to V0 - V, boosting edge density exponentially:
n_p(-x_p) = n_{p0}\,e^{V / V_T} \Rightarrow \Delta n_p = n_{p0}\!\left(e^{V / V_T} - 1\right)
I = I_0\!\left(e^{V / V_T} - 1\right),\qquad I_0 = e A\!\left(\frac{D_p\,p_{n0}}{L_p} + \frac{D_n\,n_{p0}}{L_n}\right)
WHY / Using p_{n0} = ni^2 / Nd and n_{p0} = ni^2 / Na immediately proves WHY reverse leakage I0 scales as ni^2 and why heavily doping one side suppresses its reverse injection!
WATCH / Diffusion length L_n = sqrt(Dn tau_n) is how far injected minority electrons travel before recombining; a diode needs base thicker than L_n, whereas a BJT needs W_B << L_n!

cards.title: Exact step-junction Poisson audit: 2-sided vs 1-sided (OL3/P29)
items: Audit distinction (OL3 & P29): total depletion width W = xp + xn across acceptor Na and donor Nd sides depends on REDUCED doping density N_eff:
WHY / In P29 (eps = 11.7 eps0, N = 10^21 m^-3, V0 + VR = 5.0 V, A = 1 mm^2): p+n one-sided gives W = 2.55 um, Cj = 40.7 pF; symmetric Na = Nd = N gives W = 3.60 um, Cj = 28.8 pF!
WATCH / Always state explicitly in Olympiad solutions whether you model a one-sided p^+n junction (N_eff = N) or symmetric junction (N_eff = N/2) — instant full rigor credit!

cards.title: Varactor (variable-reactance) tuning diodes & 1/C^2 law
items: Small AC signal wiggle dV around reverse bias VR charges/discharges depletion edges separated by W(VR) exactly like a voltage-controlled parallel-plate capacitor:
\frac{1}{C_j^2} = \frac{2(V_0 + V_R)}{e\,\varepsilon\,A^2 N_{\mathrm{eff}}}\ \ (\text{STRICT STRAIGHT LINE vs } V_R\text{!})
WHY / Plotting 1/Cj^2 against reverse bias VR in the lab measures BOTH built-in potential V0 (horizontal intercept -V0!) AND substrate doping N_eff (from slope)!
WATCH / Putting a varactor inside an LC tank f0 = 1 / (2 pi sqrt(L Cj)) gives f0 ~ (V0 + VR)^(+1/4) — how every PLL, FM modulator, and radio tuner tunes frequency electronically!

cards.title: Linearly graded junctions & forward diffusion capacitance
items: Not every junction is a step function! Diffused junctions with rho(x) = e a x obey a cube-root law, while forward-biased diodes add a huge storage capacitance C_diff:
\mathrm{Graded}\ \rho = e a x:\ \ W \propto (V_0 + V_R)^{1/3} \Rightarrow C_j \propto (V_0 + V_R)^{-1/3}

WHY / Stored minority charge Q_min = tau_T I takes transit/lifetime time tau_T to clear on sudden turn-off — why ordinary 1N4007 diodes fail at 100 kHz and Schottky diodes (majority carriers, tau_T ~ 0!) rule SMPS!
WATCH / Hyperabrupt varactors engineer doping N(x) ~ x^(-3/2) so Cj ~ (V0 + VR)^(-2), making LC resonant frequency f0 ~ 1/sqrt(Cj) STRICTLY LINEAR in control voltage VR!

title: Hall effect metrology, diode thermometry & 1.22 V reference
subtitle: Lorentz carrier-sign determination, two-carrier Hall zero, -2 mV/K sensor, and Brokaw bandgap circuit.
takeaway: Lorentz force deflects e- and h+ to the EXACT SAME transverse face — so Hall voltage polarity unambiguously distinguishes n-type from p-type!

cards.title: Hall effect derivation, polarity & carrier extraction (OL6)
items: Pass current I_x along +x through rectangular slab (thickness t along B_z). Magnetic force q v_d x B pushes BOTH drift electrons (v_x < 0, q = -e) and drift holes (v_x > 0, q = +e) toward the SAME face!
|E_y| = v_d B_z = \frac{J_x B_z}{n e} \Rightarrow V_H = \frac{I B}{n e t},\qquad R_H \equiv \frac{E_y}{J_x B_z} = \mp\frac{1}{n e}
WATCH / Notice slab WIDTH w cancels out of V_H = I B / (n e t)! Thin epitaxial films (tiny t) generate huge, easily measured millivolt Hall signals!

cards.title: Combining Hall + conductivity & two-carrier Hall zero
items: Conductivity alone gives ONLY the product n mu; pairing a 4-probe resistivity test with a Hall measurement extracts carrier density n AND mobility mu SEPARATELY:
R_{H,\mathrm{ambipolar}} = \frac{p\,\mu_h^2 - n\,\mu_e^2}{e(p\,\mu_h + n\,\mu_e)^2}\ \ (\text{vanishes when } p\,\mu_h^2 = n\,\mu_e^2\text{!})
WHY / Look at mu^2 in the numerator of R_H! Because mu_e = 2.81 mu_h in Si, intrinsic Si (n = p = ni) actually shows an N-TYPE negative Hall coefficient!
WATCH / Classic IPhO trap: in lightly p-doped silicon where p = (mu_e/mu_h)^2 n ~ 7.9 n, Hall voltage passes right through ZERO even though mobile carriers are abundant!

cards.title: Diode & BJT thermometer: dV_BE/dT = -2 mV/K (OL5)
items: Driving a diode-connected BJT with constant current source I_C = const and differentiating V_BE(T) = V_T ln(I_C / I_0(T)) with I_0 ~ T^3 exp(-Eg / kT):
WHY / Even though V_T = kT/e tries to raise V_BE, saturation current I_0(T) explodes exponentially across Eg, pulling V_BE DOWN linearly across -55 to +150 deg C (CTAT = Complementary To Absolute T)!
WATCH / Every CPU/GPU die embeds on-chip BJT thermal diodes reading this exact -2 mV/K slope to throttle clock frequency before silicon overheats!

cards.title: Bandgap voltage reference: cancelling CTAT + PTAT = 1.22 V
items: Run two matched BJTs at fixed current-density ratio J1 / J2 = M (e.g. M = 10): their V_BE difference eliminates I_0 completely to create a pure +T signal (PTAT):
\Delta V_{BE} = V_{BE1} - V_{BE2} = V_T\ln M = \frac{k_B\ln M}{e}\,T\ \ (\text{pure PTAT!})
WHY / Summing falling V_BE (-2 mV/K, extrapolating to Eg/e at 0 K) + amplified rising K*dV_BE (+2 mV/K) locks V_ref right onto silicon's extrapolated 0 K bandgap ~1.22-1.25 V (P34)!
WATCH / Every precision IC regulator (LM317's famous 1.25 V reference, ADC refs, phone PMICs) rests directly on this CTAT + PTAT cancellation!

title: Shockley-Queisser PV bound, shaded strings & tandem cells
subtitle: Spectral loss trade-off (~33.7% at 1.34 eV), tandem solar stacks, hotspot physics, and bypass diodes.
takeaway: Single-junction PV cells lose sub-gap red photons (unabsorbed) and excess above-gap blue energy (phonons), capping 1-sun efficiency near ~33.7% at Eg ~ 1.34 eV!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md OL4, OL10, P30, P35

cards.title: Two fundamental spectral losses in single-junction PV (OL4)
items: Sunlight spans ~0.4 to 4.0 eV (~5800 K blackbody). A single semiconductor bandgap Eg extracts EXACTLY Eg (minus recombination loss) per absorbed photon:
h\nu > E_g:\ \text{excess }(h\nu - E_g)\text{ lost as phonons}
WHY / Tiny Eg absorbs everything but delivers tiny V_oc < Eg/e; huge Eg gives large V_oc but wastes nearly all solar photons -> product peaks sharply around Eg ~ 1.34 eV!
WATCH / In P30 Olympiad answers, you MUST name BOTH spectral losses PLUS radiative recombination (which forces V_oc < Eg/e and FF < 1) to derive the ~33.7% ceiling!

cards.title: Why crystalline Si (1.12 eV) dominates & how tandems beat 33%
items: Silicon's 1.12 eV gap sits right beside the broad SQ plateau (~32% theoretical limit; ~27% lab record), backed by abundant SiO2 sand and wafer purity.
WHY / Top wide-gap subcell harvests blue/green photons at HIGH voltage (~1.2 V) while letting red/IR pass transparently down into bottom Si subcell — crushing thermalisation loss!
WATCH / Focusing sunlight with lenses/mirrors (concentrator PV, C suns) boosts I_L -> raises V_oc by V_T ln C, lifting theoretical infinite-junction limit toward 86.8%!

cards.title: Shaded series solar cell hotspot crisis (OL10 & P35)
items: Solar modules wire N cells (e.g. 60 or 72) IN SERIES so voltages add to ~35-40 V. If ONE single leaf shades cell #k, KCL forces identical current through every cell:
I_{\mathrm{str}} > I_{L,\mathrm{sh}} \Rightarrow V_{\mathrm{shaded}} = V_{\mathrm{load}} - \sum_{j\neq k} V_j < 0
P_{\mathrm{hotspot}} = |V_{\mathrm{shaded}}|\,I_{\mathrm{string}}\ \ (\text{tens of watts in ONE cell!})
WHY / All N - 1 sunlit cells gang up like a 30 V battery ramming 8 A BACKWARD into the one shaded cell — baking EVA encapsulant and cracking glass!
WATCH / Without protection, either open-circuit load drops string power to the worst cell OR low load resistance drives destructive reverse avalanche breakdown!

cards.title: Antiparallel bypass diodes & stepped multi-peak I-V curves
items: Wiring a Schottky bypass diode in ANTI-PARALLEL across each sub-string of M cells (typically 20-24 cells per diode, 3 diodes per 60/72-cell panel) saves both power and hardware:
WHY / Full 8 A string current detours cleanly around the shaded sub-string: the module loses ONLY 1/3 of voltage (~65% power saved!) instead of collapsing by 80-90%!
WATCH / Signature on panel I(V) curve (P35c): K distinct current steps / local power peaks — which is why solar inverters run global MPPT sweeps!

title: Shot noise, Johnson noise, NEP & LED load-line stability
subtitle: Poisson discrete-charge floor, resistor thermal noise, minimum detectable power, and OL9 design.
takeaway: Shot noise i_rms = sqrt(2 e I df) comes from discrete charge quanta e; Johnson noise i_th = sqrt(4 kT df / R) comes from thermal agitation — add variances i_tot^2 = i_shot^2 + i_th^2!

cards.title: Quantum shot noise from Poisson arrival statistics (OL8, P32)
items: Current I consists of discrete independent electrons e crossing a potential barrier at mean rate N / tau = I / e. Over observation window tau = 1 / (2 df), count variance is N:
\sigma_I^2 = \left(\frac{e}{\tau}\right)^{\!2} N = \frac{e^2}{\tau^2}\!\left(\frac{I\tau}{e}\right) = 2 e I\,\Delta f \Rightarrow i_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{2 e I\,\Delta f}
WHY / OL8 & P32 checks: (1) I = 1 uA, df = 1 MHz => i_rms = 0.566 nA; (2) I = 4 uA, df = 2 MHz => i_rms = 1.60 nA! Narrowing receiver bandwidth df by 4x cuts rms noise in HALF!
WATCH / Dark current I_d and background light I_bg add uncorrelated shot noise even when signal modulates around zero: total shot variance is 2 e (I_sig + I_dark + I_bg) df!

cards.title: Johnson-Nyquist resistor noise & photoreceiver SNR / NEP
items: Load resistor R_L at temperature T adds thermal Johnson current noise independent of DC current; total receiver noise sums mean-square powers:
i_{n,\mathrm{tot}} = \sqrt{\bigl(2 e(I_{\mathrm{photo}} + I_{\mathrm{dark}}) + \frac{4 k_B T}{R_L}\bigr)\Delta f}
WHY / Shot noise beats thermal noise once I*R_L > 2 k_B T / e = 51.7 mV! Any voltage drop > 52 mV across load resistor R_L puts the receiver in the quantum shot-noise regime!
WATCH / Never add rms currents linearly (i1 + i2)! Independent Gaussian/Poisson noise sources ALWAYS add IN QUADRATURE: sqrt(i_shot^2 + i_thermal^2)!

cards.title: Why LEDs MUST have current-limiting ballast (OL9)
items: An LED is an exponential diode (I ~ exp(V / VT)), NOT an ohmic bulb! Connecting a 2.0 V LED directly across a stiff voltage rail invites instant thermal runaway:
R_{\mathrm{series}} = \frac{V_{CC} - V_{\mathrm{LED}}}{I_{\mathrm{target}}}\ \ \Bigl(\mathrm{OL9:}\ \frac{5.0 - 2.0\text{ V}}{20\text{ mA}} = 150\ \Omega,\ P_R = 60\text{ mW}\Bigr)
WHY / Without R_series, a +100 mV supply bump or +50 K junction warm-up (-100 mV knee shift!) boosts LED current by 10^(100/60) ~ 46x — melting the bond wire in milliseconds!
WATCH / Never wire two bare LEDs directly IN PARALLEL off one shared resistor! The slightly warmer LED drops V_LED by 2 mV/K, hogs all current, overheats further, and cascades to destruction!

cards.title: Small-signal sensitivity: voltage source vs series resistor
items: Compare fractional current sensitivity dI / I to a diode knee shift dV_LED under stiff voltage drive vs resistor-ballasted drive:
\mathrm{Stiff\ V\ drive:}\ \ \frac{\delta I}{I} = -\frac{\delta V_{\mathrm{LED}}}{V_T} \approx -39\times\delta V_{\mathrm{LED}}\ (\text{in volts!})
\mathrm{With\ } R_s:\ \ \frac{\delta I}{I} = -\frac{\delta V_{\mathrm{LED}}}{I R_s + V_T} \approx -\frac{\delta V_{\mathrm{LED}}}{V_{CC} - V_{\mathrm{LED}}}\ \ (\text{115x gentler!})
WHY / Dropping 3.0 V across R_s makes loop slope resistance I R_s + V_T = 3.026 V instead of 0.026 V — turning a wild exponential device into a rock-steady 3% current source!
WATCH / High-power white LED headlamps replace wasteful series resistors with buck switch-mode constant-current drivers (>92% efficiency vs 40% linear resistor)!

title: Moore's quantum wall, oxide tunnelling & chip heat budget
subtitle: Heisenberg confinement spread, WKB gate leakage, high-k FinFETs, and 500-800 W CMOS power.
takeaway: Charging capacitor C through resistor to VDD draws CV^2 from battery: 1/2 CV^2 stored, 1/2 CV^2 burned on rise + 1/2 CV^2 burned on discharge = CV^2 per full 0->1->0 cycle!
source: Source: semiconductors/Semiconductors.md sec. 3.13, OL7, OL11, P31, P36 & CMOS cycle audit

cards.title: Quantum wall #1: Heisenberg confinement energy (OL7, P31)
items: Squeezing channel/well dimension dx to a few nanometres gives carriers minimum zero-point kinetic energy spread via dx * dp >= hbar:
\Delta E \sim \frac{\hbar^2}{2 m_e(\Delta x)^2}:\ 1.5\text{ meV }(5\text{ nm}),\ 4.2\text{ meV }(3\text{ nm})
\text{With } m^* = 0.19\,m_e:\ \Delta E(3\text{ nm}) \approx 22\text{ meV} \sim k_B T
WHY / Carrier de Broglie wavelength at 300 K is h / sqrt(3 m* kT) ~ 12 nm — smaller than a modern transistor pitch, so 2D/1D quantum subbands replace bulk classical drift!
WATCH / Quote BOTH free-electron mass result (4.2 meV at 3 nm, P31a exact!) AND note that light effective mass m* raises confinement right up to thermal kT = 26 meV!

cards.title: Quantum wall #2: WKB gate-oxide tunnelling leakage
items: Scaling planar MOSFET capacitance C_ox = eps_ox A / d_ox once forced SiO2 thickness down to d_ox ~ 1.2 nm (~5 atomic layers!), where WKB tunnelling explodes:
WHY / Every 0.2 nm thinning multiplies gate leakage current by ~10x! At 1.2 nm, 10^9 "OFF" transistors leak tens of amps straight through the gate insulator!
WATCH / How did semiconductor physics beat both walls (P31c)? (1) High-k HfO2 (kappa ~ 25 vs 3.9 -> 6x thicker physical wall for same C_ox!) + (2) 3D FinFET / Gate-All-Around nanosheets!

cards.title: CMOS capacitor charging energetics & cycle audit (OL11, P36)
items: Reconciling single-transition vs full-cycle formulas cleanly from exact capacitor physics:
\text{Full cycle }(0\to 1\to 0):\ P_{\mathrm{dyn}} = \alpha_{\mathrm{sw}} N C V_{DD}^2 f
WHY / Audit clarity: if N gates each make 1 transition per clock period (activity alpha_sw = 0.5), P = (1/2) N C V^2 f = 500 W (OL11: N=10^9, f=1 GHz, C=1 fF, V=1 V) & 810 W (P36)!
WATCH / Making transistor channel R -> 0 does NOT reduce switching energy 1/2 CV^2 — it only burns the exact same 1/2 CV^2 faster in shorter RC time!

cards.title: Why CPU clocks stalled near ~4-5 GHz (Dennard breakdown)
items: Total chip thermal dissipation combines dynamic switching power plus subthreshold leakage across billions of transistors:
P_{\mathrm{total}} = \alpha_{\mathrm{sw}} N C V_{DD}^2 f + N\,V_{DD}\,I_0\,e^{-V_{\mathrm{th}} / (\eta V_T)}
